title: Pi Agent · Kernel Optimization
subtitle: Batched multi-LoRA shrink/expand: four submissions, a cache regression, and a return to the best code
scope: Tracks "Git tree of submitted candidates, submission number, final selection status". Scratch tests, unsubmitted edits, and failed attempts are expanded at the behavior level; this does not represent a full machine snapshot after every file write. The version tree represents code provenance, the timeline represents actual chronological order; branches do not indicate parallelism.
notes: Pi Agent run 20261001-r1: DeepSeek model ID deepseek-flash, thinking level high (session.jsonl, lines 2–3). Task wro-lora-punica-fused-loop16 optimizes batched multi-LoRA shrink/expand in three editable vLLM files, preserving signatures and outputs within 2% relative tolerance with fp16 inputs and fp32 accumulation (main:E1).

Recorded environment: one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (40,960 MiB), Python 3.10.12, PyTorch 2.7.1+cu126, Triton 3.3.1, installed vLLM 0.10.1.1; CUDA build 12.6 (main:E30, main:E35 and session.jsonl line 5). Budget: 5,400 seconds / 90 minutes, at most 16 sequential submissions; observed session 44.63 minutes with four submissions. No separate reviewer session is present. The record gives the model alias, not an immutable provider model revision.

Status colors are based on dev_speedup changes between adjacent submissions. Submission 3 passed correctness but had a lower score; submission 4 restored v2 kernel_utils and continued editing, with the version tree branching from submission 2.

Independent Oracle paired score 2.113798×, independent official baseline score 34.588125×, and dev_speedup 35.444980× are recorded separately and are not interchangeable. The final selection card references the historical dev_speedup, not a new measurement.

No independent reviewer trajectory this round; among the 150 tool calls there were no Skill-loading calls or main-text reads. Skills listed as installed/in directory do not equal actual usage, so no Skill or Review nodes are fabricated.
No explicit Wiki/TODO lifecycle record. Experience read/write only shows scratch code copies that were actually saved and read; this cannot be used to claim the Wiki mechanism was used.

The six behavior categories and English annotations are analyst-labeled; full reasoning, utterances, tool inputs, outputs, and diagnostic attachments remain at the original text layer. Multiple results from the same call are grouped under that call; asynchronous execution and later result retrieval are kept separate.

A command returning success does not automatically mean verification passed; Tracebacks, BAD results, schema rejections, interrupted background scans, and post-failure fixes are each annotated separately. The Token field is the cumulative session input count, not a single node's consumption.
This public example preserves the previously exported session and scoring attachments. Historical tool names and paths remain verbatim in the raw record; the displayed agent name is Pi Agent.

states.title: Baseline
states.summary: Pi Agent starts from Python code that loops over LoRA adapters and performs separate matrix operations. It must accelerate batched shrink/expand while preserving fp16 inputs, fp32 accumulation and 2% relative tolerance. Only three vLLM files are editable. Before submitting a change, the agent saves the baseline, builds an fp64 reference and checks ten local cases. These scratch activities remain under the baseline state because states track submitted code and final selection.

ladder.takeaway: Python baseline needs milliseconds per call before grouped kernels
ladder.reason: Scratch checks establish a local reference. States track submitted code, so pre-submission experiments remain here.

states.title: V1 · Grouped kernel
states.summary: Submission 1 replaces the Python adapter loop with grouped Triton shrink and expand kernels. The development evaluator reports correctness PASS and 18.671× speedup against its baseline. Local tests also pass, but timing changes when diagnostic instrumentation is disabled. The agent therefore separates GPU execution from host launch cost before choosing its next optimization.

lineage.reason: Continued modifying along the current candidate and submitted; the subsequent candidate in the same timeline.

ladder.takeaway: Grouped kernels pass correctness at 18.67× development speedup
ladder.reason: Submission 1 removes the adapter loop. Host launch becomes the next measured target.

states.title: V2 · Direct launch
states.summary: Submission 2 adds direct calls to CompiledKernel, cheaper CUDA stream lookup and measured tile settings. The development score rises from 18.671× to 33.369×, with correctness PASS. A local breakdown measures about 21.65 µs per operation after the host changes. The agent saves this code for comparison and possible restoration before trying object-identity caching.

lineage.reason: Continued modifying along the current candidate and submitted; the subsequent candidate in the same timeline.

assessment.note: dev_speedup in the same round's submission receipt; color only indicates measured value change, not statistical significance.

ladder.takeaway: Direct launch and raw stream raise development speedup to 33.37×
ladder.reason: Submission 2 passes correctness. The agent saves this code before trying identity caching.

states.title: V3 · Identity cache
states.summary: Submission 3 retains an object-identity cache and slice-offset changes. CUDA Graph caching was tried and removed before this submission. Local A/B tests with reused tensors favor the candidate, but the development score falls from 33.369× to 30.834×; correctness still passes. Subsequent fresh and rotating object tests expose a cache limitation. They suggest a possible explanation for the regression, but do not reveal the evaluator's actual input pattern.

lineage.reason: Continued modifying along the current candidate and submitted; the subsequent candidate in the same timeline.

assessment.note: dev_speedup in the same round's submission receipt; color only indicates measured value change, not statistical significance.

ladder.takeaway: Identity cache passes correctness but development speedup falls to 30.83×
ladder.reason: Reused-object local tests were faster. Later fresh and rotating object tests expose a limitation.

states.title: V4 · New specialization key
states.summary: The agent restores submission 2's kernel_utils.py and builds a cheaper specialization key on that code. It retains slice offsets, fixes a function-signature mismatch and handles floating-point arguments separately from integer alignment checks. Local rotating-object timing falls from 22.04 to 19.74 µs; stable-object timing falls from 21.58 to 19.30 µs. Submission 4 passes correctness and reaches 35.445× development speedup. Its code derives from submission 2, although it occurs after submission 3.

lineage.reason: The command restored v2_33.37/kernel_utils.py and immediately continued editing; the final hashes of both wrappers match v2. This is a new version built on v2, not an unmodified restoration.

assessment.note: dev_speedup in the same round's submission receipt; color only indicates measured value change, not statistical significance.

ladder.takeaway: Simpler key built from submission 2 reaches 35.44× development speedup
ladder.reason: Signature and float-dispatch fixes restore correctness. Both measured object patterns improve locally.

states.title: Final · Select V4
states.summary: The agent restores and finalizes submission 4 after a later alignment variant measures slightly slower locally. The three final file hashes match the saved submission 4 copy. The retained development score is 35.445×; finalization is not a new measurement. Separate evaluation confirms correctness and reports 34.588× against the official baseline and 2.114× against the frozen Oracle under paired ABBA evaluation. These scores use different baselines.

lineage.reason: Discarded the unsubmitted alignment specialization experiment, restored v4 files, and finalized the selection of submission 4; no 5th submission was produced.

assessment.note: The final selection references submission 4's dev_speedup; independent scores are listed separately in the measurement record.

ladder.takeaway: Selected submission 4 passes independent correctness and records 2.11× against Oracle
ladder.reason: Development score remains 35.44×. Independent official-baseline speedup is 34.59×; these baselines differ.

First I'll snapshot the baseline into scratch as my own reference, then write the new implementation.

branches.title: Own reference and baseline
branches.summary: The agent writes an fp64 reference and ten local correctness and timing cases. An import error initially prevents the scratch copy from running. After fixing module loading, the baseline passes all ten cases and takes roughly 2.7 to 17 ms per operator with diagnostics enabled. These measurements establish the local comparison point; they are separate from the development evaluator.

ladder.takeaway: Local baseline passes ten cases and takes 2.7 to 17 ms per operator
ladder.reason: Diagnostics are enabled in this timing. An import fix enables the scratch fp64 comparison.

branches.title: Grouped Triton kernel
branches.summary: The agent writes grouped Triton kernels and connects both shrink and expand entry points to them. All ten local cases pass against the fp64 reference. Many timings cluster near 200 µs despite different workloads. The agent suspects a host or instrumentation cost and investigates that cost before treating these timings as kernel performance.

ladder.takeaway: Grouped kernels pass ten local cases; timing still needs diagnosis
ladder.reason: Different shapes cluster near 200 µs while diagnostic instrumentation is active.

abstract.quote: Baseline measured (~5-17 ms per op). Now let me run my new implementation.

branches.title: Distinguishing GPU vs. host cost
branches.summary: With diagnostics disabled, the agent compares ordinary calls, CUDA Graph replay and host profiles. One shrink call takes about 64 µs, while a later breakdown attributes about 45 µs to Triton launch. Device timings depend on shape and are measured separately. An early launch bypass fails with a grid error. The agent submits the working grouped kernel before continuing host-path changes.

ladder.takeaway: Host launch remains costly after grouped kernels reduce device work
ladder.reason: The agent disables instrumentation, separates device timing and profiles Triton specialization.

abstract.quote: every case reports ≈200 µs regardless of size
Pure device time is 19-220 µs, but there's a ~45 µs/call host launch overhead floor.

branches.title: Submission and official feedback
branches.summary: The agent submits the grouped Triton implementation after local correctness checks. The asynchronous evaluator returns correctness PASS and dev_speedup 18.671×. This is submission 1 of the allowed 16; the next work investigates the remaining host cost.

ladder.takeaway: Submission 1 passes correctness at 18.67× development speedup
ladder.reason: This is the first evaluator receipt. Fifteen submission attempts remain.

branches.title: Tile parameter experiments on the same kernel
branches.summary: The agent searches tile sizes and launch parameters for the same grouped kernels. It stops a broad sweep, then discovers that a background sweep ended with its shell and left partial results. It runs a smaller foreground sweep to obtain comparable results. Different shapes favor different tiles; the retained implementation uses measured settings for shrink and expand.

ladder.takeaway: Tile search moves to a smaller foreground sweep after incomplete runs
ladder.reason: A broad sweep is stopped; a background sweep ends with its shell. The completed scan compares four shapes.

abstract.quote: The background tuner died with its shell session. Let me run a small, focused sweep in the foreground.

branches.title: Directly launching the compiled kernel
branches.summary: A first direct-launch experiment supplies 26 arguments where the launcher requires 32, so it fails. The agent inspects the actual launcher signature and repeats the test with the full argument set. Direct launch takes 17.32 µs versus 43.76 µs for the normal path, with bitwise-identical output in that test. It integrates this path and keeps guards around argument packing.

ladder.takeaway: Direct launch takes 17.32 µs versus 43.76 µs with identical test output
ladder.reason: The first attempt had missing arguments. Reading the real signature enables a valid comparison.

abstract.quote: a direct `CompiledKernel` launch cuts 44 µs → 17 µs with bitwise-identical output.

branches.title: Streamlining the host path
branches.summary: After direct launch passes the local cases, the agent profiles the remaining wrapper, key construction and stream lookup. A scratch test with fabricated strides fails and is corrected. The raw stream accessor takes 0.23 µs versus 6.33 µs for current_stream(). The agent changes stream lookup and trims stride arguments; the full operation then measures 21.65 µs locally.

ladder.takeaway: Raw stream lookup takes 0.23 µs versus current_stream at 6.33 µs
ladder.reason: Changing the accessor and stride handling lowers the full local call to 21.65 µs.

abstract.quote: The raw-stream API is 27× cheaper (0.23 µs vs 6.3 µs).

branches.title: Submission and official feedback
branches.summary: Submission 2 combines direct launch, raw stream lookup and tile choices. The evaluator reports correctness PASS and 33.369× development speedup, up from submission 1's 18.671×. The agent saves this candidate before further experiments.

ladder.takeaway: Submission 2 passes correctness at 33.37× development speedup
ladder.reason: The agent saves the improved direct-launch code for comparison and restoration.

branches.title: Identity-based launch parameter caching
branches.summary: The agent caches launch arguments by tensor identity. Its first implementation launches twice on a cache miss and breaks add_inputs; an initial fix also skips required work. Restructuring the control flow restores correctness. Early cache-hit instrumentation shows hits without a clear full-call gain. A later, simplified version with slice offsets is 3 to 5 µs faster in local A/B tests that reuse tensors, so the agent submits it for development scoring.

ladder.takeaway: Identity caching gains depend on the implementation and object reuse
ladder.reason: Double launches first break accumulation. After repair and simplification, reused-object A/B tests favor the candidate.

abstract.quote: Clean A/B shows the current version is ~3-5 µs/op faster than round 2 on every shape.

branches.title: CUDA Graph and reducing views
branches.summary: A standalone CUDA Graph replay takes 5 µs versus 21 µs for the direct-call test. After integration, fresh slice views cause repeated captures, so the agent passes slice offsets instead and limits capture. The agent then estimates only about 2 µs net benefit and removes the graph path. The standalone replay result does not establish an equal gain for the full operator.

ladder.takeaway: CUDA Graph replay is fast alone; integration leaves little net benefit
ladder.reason: The agent estimates about 2 µs saved after key overhead and removes the graph path.

abstract.quote: Graphs only save ~2 µs net here (the key overhead eats the replay gain) — not worth the risk.

branches.title: Submission and official feedback
branches.summary: The evaluator accepts submission 3's numerical behavior but reports 30.834× development speedup. Submission 2 remains best at 33.369×. The result conflicts with the local reused-tensor A/B result, which motivates a comparison of input-object patterns.

ladder.takeaway: Submission 3 stays correct but regresses to 30.83× development speedup
ladder.reason: Submission 2 remains best at 33.37× despite the favorable local reused-object test.

branches.title: Compared call patterns to explain the regression
branches.summary: The original identity cache takes 17.01 µs with stable objects versus 21.89 µs for submission 2, but takes 65.46 µs with fresh objects versus 61.08 µs for submission 2. The fresh-object totals include allocation. An adaptive miss policy still takes 24.68 µs on rotating objects versus 22.41 µs for submission 2. The agent abandons the identity approach. The evaluator's actual object-reuse pattern remains unobserved.

ladder.takeaway: Object reuse changes whether identity caching helps
ladder.reason: Fresh-object totals include allocation. Rotating objects also disfavor the candidate; the evaluator input pattern is unknown.

abstract.quote: Round 3 scored **30.83** vs round 2's 33.37, despite being 3-5 µs/op faster locally with *reused* tensors.
The evidence suggests the harness may pass new tensor objects each call (so an identity cache never hits but still costs).

branches.title: Redid the specialization key starting from v2
branches.summary: The agent copies kernel_utils.py from submission 2 and rewrites the specialization key, while retaining slice offsets. The first retest exposes an outdated function signature; a later test exposes a bitwise operation on a float. After both fixes, correctness passes and rotating/stable object tests favor the new implementation. A stale microbenchmark fails separately, so the entire command is not labeled as a clean success.

ladder.takeaway: Submission 2 code supplies the base for a cheaper specialization key
ladder.reason: The agent retains slice offsets and fixes signature and float-dispatch errors before submission.

abstract.quote: Round 3's identity cache didn't pay off in the harness.

branches.title: Submission and official feedback
branches.summary: Submission 4 passes correctness and reaches 35.445× development speedup. This exceeds both the previous submission's 30.834× and submission 2's 33.369×. The agent then broadens local boundary tests before deciding whether to continue optimizing.

ladder.takeaway: Submission 4 passes correctness and reaches 35.44× development speedup
ladder.reason: It exceeds both submission 3 and its code ancestor, submission 2.

abstract.quote: the new version is ~2.3 µs/op faster in *both* the fresh-tensor and stable-tensor patterns (19.7 µs vs 22.0 µs).

branches.title: Boundary condition validation
branches.summary: The agent tests nineteen boundary cases, including bf16, fp32 fallback, small/large ranks, noncontiguous views, offsets and add_inputs. An offset test first fails because the reference script creates the wrong output shape. After fixing that script, all nineteen cases pass. This expands local correctness coverage; it is not a new development or independent performance score.

ladder.takeaway: Boundary tests all pass after the reference shape is fixed
ladder.reason: Nineteen local cases cover dtypes, ranks, offsets, views and routing. This is correctness coverage.

branches.title: Further overhead localization
branches.summary: A direct-launch microbenchmark compares six arguments with twenty-one. Timing rises from 6.04 to 6.47 µs, about 0.029 µs per extra argument. The agent explicitly stops trimming arguments after seeing this small local contribution.

ladder.takeaway: Argument count adds about 0.029 µs per extra direct-launch argument
ladder.reason: The agent stops trimming arguments after the six-versus-twenty-one comparison.

abstract.quote: direct launch  6 args:  6.04us   21 args:  6.47us   -> 0.029us per extra argument

branches.title: Alternative approach removing alignment specialization
branches.summary: The agent saves submission 4 and tries skipping alignment specialization. Correctness passes, but rotating-object timing is 20.60 µs versus 20.32 µs for the saved candidate; stable-object timing also worsens slightly. It restores the saved files and does not submit this variant. The restoration receipt includes passing test output while the command is still running; the final hash audit is recorded later.

ladder.takeaway: Alignment variant is slightly slower locally, so submission 4 is restored
ladder.reason: Correctness passes. No development score is submitted for this variant.

abstract.quote: The extra alignment-specialization skip measured slightly *slower* — reverting to the verified best version.

branches.title: Restoring the best version and finalizing the submission
branches.summary: The first finalize request contains an unsupported tool argument and is rejected before execution. The corrected request succeeds and explicitly selects submission 4 at 4 of 16 allowed submissions. This records the chosen artifact; separate evaluation supplies the independent scores.

ladder.takeaway: Finalize selects submission 4 after a rejected first request
ladder.reason: The first tool call never executes. Corrected arguments produce an explicit selection receipt.

abstract.quote: Final state verified (10/10 benchmark cases + 19/19 robustness cases pass). Let me finalize.

branches.title: Final code verification and summary
branches.summary: The agent checks the final functions and hashes of all three editable files. They match the saved submission 4 copy, while HEAD remains the original baseline commit with those files modified. The final narrative explains local results and rejected attempts. ladder.reason: HEAD remains the baseline commit with three modified files. The final narrative is kept as an agent report.

The final summary from the original session.
Pure device time is far below wall-clock time, so the investigation shifted to reading the Triton launch path to find the overhead.
Each sample took about 200 µs, prompting disabling diagnostics to retest host cost.
Confirmed device time was already small enough to submit the first version.
Host-layer measurements showed launch took 44.69 µs, so direct launch was written into the candidate
Fast launch took 17 µs and was bitwise consistent, so it was written into the candidate
Foreground scan gave the best tile, so it was written into the config
raw stream was 27x cheaper than current_stream, so switched to using it
Local cost dropped to 21.65 µs and passed, so submitted version 2
Alias miss measurements led the agent to instrument the scratch copy to count hits
Replay measured at 5 µs vs 21 µs led the agent to decide to implement Graph caching
Multi-slice qkv slowdown led the agent to pass slice offset instead to stabilize the Graph key
Graph only saved about 2 µs, so it was removed, keeping the simpler fast path
A/B testing of reused objects showed faster results, based on which the agent submitted version 3
Version 3's score regression triggered subsequent fresh vs rotating object comparisons
Fresh objects were actually slower, prompting addition of adaptive disabling
Rotating was still slower than v2, so identity caching was abandoned and reverted to v2
Per-parameter cost was extremely low, so reducing parameter count was stopped in favor of trying alignment
Removing alignment was locally slightly slower, so version 4 was restored

{"type":"message","id":"dcfb45ba","parentId":"d11788c3","timestamp":"2026-10-01T10:13:49.780Z","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Performance Optimization Task

## Objective
A multi-LoRA batched apply subsystem (the shrink → expand path) in this repository is
functionally correct but slow. Make it **faster** on the benchmark workloads while
**preserving its numerical behavior** (outputs within a **2% relative tolerance**;
fp16 inputs, fp32 accumulation). All work must stay inside the declared editable scope.

## Editable scope
Edit **only** these three files (edits outside this scope score the submission zero):
```
vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/kernel_utils.py
vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py
vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_expand_op.py
```

## Entry points and contract
Two registered ops drive the subsystem:
- `lora_shrink(inputs, lora_a_weights, output_tensor, token_lora_mapping, token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids, num_tokens_per_lora, lora_token_start_loc, lora_ids, no_lora_flag_cpu, scaling)` — for each token, projects it through its assigned LoRA's A matrix (scaled). `output_tensor` `[num_slices, num_tokens, rank]` is written in place.
- `lora_expand(inputs, lora_b_weights, output_tensor, ...same routing..., offset_start=0, add_inputs=False)` — projects the shrunk buffer through the LoRA's B matrix into the output slice region (adding when `add_inputs`). `output_tensor` `[num_tokens, sum-of-slice-out-sizes]` is written in place.
- Each token carries a LoRA id via `token_lora_mapping` (`-1` = no LoRA); the routing tensors group tokens by LoRA id. `lora_a_weights[s]`: `[num_loras, rank, hidden]`; `lora_b_weights[s]`: `[num_loras, out, rank]`.

**Correctness requirement.** For every benchmark input, the outputs must match the
reference LoRA result within a **2% relative tolerance**. Any change altering the
result beyond that tolerance scores zero.

## Workload shape
The benchmark drives batched multi-LoRA application: thousands of tokens each routed
to one of several LoRA adapters, small adapter rank, shrink then expand. A hidden set
covers additional shapes.

## Rules
- Preserve the ops' signatures and behavior (within tolerance).
- Do **not** read, run, reproduce, or infer the scoring/verifier code, hidden test
  workloads, thresholds, or any reference solution.
- Do **not** download, clone, fetch, or otherwise obtain the upstream project, its
  history, or any external reference implementation, and do **not** bypass or disable
  the network isolation. Solve from the code present. Any such action scores the whole task zero.
- Write the optimization **in these three files**, using the libraries they already
  import (PyTorch / Triton). Do **not** copy or recover an implementation from any other
  copy of this package inside the container (for example an installed
  `site-packages`/`dist-packages` copy, a version-control object store, or another module
  of the repository), and do **not** load code from outside the declared scope at run time
  (`importlib`, `spec_from_file_location`, `exec`, or shelling out via
  `subprocess`/`os.system`/`os.popen`). A submission whose in-scope code does any of this
  scores zero.

## 🔁 Iterative submission protocol (this task uses a per-task loop)

### 1. Goal + protocol

Optimize the performance of *this* task as far as you can. You have a
**submission budget of 1 to 16**: you may submit as few as **1** time and at
most **16** (hard ceiling). There is no minimum beyond a single submission and
no requirement to keep going — finalize as soon as you judge your solution good
enough.

**Iterate ONE round at a time, feedback-driven.** Each round is a single cycle:

1. **Edit** one of the in-scope files (`/app/repo/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/kernel_utils.py`, `/app/repo/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py`, `/app/repo/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_expand_op.py`) — apply ONE concrete change based on your current
   hypothesis (round 1: based on reading the baseline code).
2. **Submit** by running `bash /opt/loop/submit.sh` **once** — it returns
   sanitized correctness + `dev_speedup` + `best_so_far` + `remaining` +
   `finalize_allowed` synchronously.
3. **Read the feedback in full.** If correctness FAIL, the named failing
   invariant is your fix target. If PASS, `dev_speedup` vs `best_so_far`
   tells you whether this round improved.
4. **Analyze in writing** — (a) what the feedback told you, (b) *why* this
   round's change had that effect (mechanistic reasoning), (c) *what specific
   single change* the next round will try.
5. **Edit again based on that analysis**, then go to step 2.

Do **NOT** call `submit.sh` in a batch; do **NOT** plan more than one attempt
ahead — round `k+1`'s plan must depend on round `k`'s measured outcome. Edit
only product code; never touch tests/benchmarks/workloads/build files.

If the feedback ever says `harness_error`, that submission was refunded and
the failure is NOT your code's fault — do not debug the harness; retry or
continue optimizing.

### 2. Termination

Two ways to end:

- (a) reach 16 submissions (auto-finalize triggers as a safety net); or
- (b) at any k with **1 ≤ k < 16**, once you believe you have reached your
  practical/theoretical limit (e.g. the last few submissions converged within
  run noise), run
  `bash /opt/loop/submit.sh --finalize --reason "<one concrete sentence on
  why you are stopping>"` — the reason is recorded and audited.

Early exit is a feature: you keep the best of your submissions, and a
*justified* stop scores exactly the same as burning all 16. You decide when to
stop; there is no minimum submission count.

### 3. 🔴 Red line (hard — ANY one of these ⇒ the whole task scores 0 in audit)

The scoring machinery is protected and off-limits. Solve this task
**independently**: rely ONLY on the code in `/app/repo`, the sanitized feedback
`submit` returns, and your own knowledge and reasoning.

- Do **NOT deliberately** read, `cat`, `open`, `less`, `head`/`tail`, `grep`,
  `find`, or edit ANY verifier / correctness / timing / scoring / hidden-test
  file or directory, wherever it lives. Executing `bash /opt/loop/submit.sh` is
  the ONLY sanctioned interaction with the scoring machinery.
- Do **NOT** run the verifier directly or try to reproduce / reverse-engineer
  it — score **only** by calling `bash /opt/loop/submit.sh`.
- Do **NOT** search for, print, or infer the hidden workloads, seeds,
  thresholds, the metric name, or the reference speedup from any source.
- Do **NOT** fetch or look up an upstream implementation or a reference
  solution (no web search, no `git` remote fetch, no network to the source),
  whether internet is on or off.
- Do **NOT** use, quote, or condition your code on any verifier / scoring /
  source material, however you came to see it.
- Do **NOT** call or reference the banned route-around tokens (`site-packages`, `dist-packages`, `importlib`, `spec_from_file_location`, `import_module`, `subprocess`, `os.system`, `os.popen`, `exec(`, `.git/`, `gated_gelu`, `ops.torch_ops`, `ops.xla_ops`) anywhere in your submitted code — the verifier scans your three scope files textually for these tokens and scores the task 0 on a hit. Build the shrink/expand path yourself, inside the scope files, from the code already present; do not dynamically load or copy an implementation from anywhere else in the container.

Stay inside `/app/repo` and scratch directories you created yourself; use only
what `submit` returns for scoring signal.

### 4. 🎓 Explain for a beginner — per round, not in bulk

Before your first edit, explain your **approach** (the hypothesis round 1
tests). Then **after every `submit.sh` feedback — and BEFORE the next edit —**
give a step-by-step analysis: what the result told you, *why* the change had
that effect, and *what single change* you will try next, written so an
undergraduate can follow.

## 提交方式

会话内用 `bash /opt/loop/submit.sh` 自评并拿反馈,完成后 `bash /opt/loop/submit.sh --finalize`。
改动留在工作树里,不需要 `git commit`。

---

## Run context (appended by the fai_bench runner; not part of the task statement)

- Environment: this container. Working directory: `/app/repo`.
- Graded working tree: `/app/repo`.
- Editable scope declared by the task: `vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/kernel_utils.py`, `vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py`, `vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_expand_op.py`. Editing anything else can trip the scope gate and zero the score.
- Leave your work in the WORKING TREE. Do **not** `git commit` and do not move `HEAD`: grading diffs the working tree against the baked baseline commit, and a moved `HEAD` makes even a correct solution score 0.

import torch

from vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops.utils import _get_lora_a_ptr
from vllm.platforms import current_platform
from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
from vllm.utils import direct_register_custom_op



def _lora_shrink_kernel(*args, **kwargs):

def _lora_shrink(
    inputs: torch.Tensor,
    lora_a_weights: list[torch.Tensor],
    output_tensor: torch.Tensor,
    token_lora_mapping: torch.Tensor,
    token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids: torch.Tensor,
    num_tokens_per_lora: torch.Tensor,
    lora_token_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
    lora_ids: torch.Tensor,
    no_lora_flag_cpu: torch.Tensor,
    scaling: float,
) -> None:
    # Straightforward shrink: for each (slice, token) with an assigned LoRA id,
    # project the token through that LoRA's A matrix and scale. output_tensor is
    # [num_slices, num_tokens, rank] and is written in place. Tokens are grouped
    # by LoRA id one id at a time.
    if bool(no_lora_flag_cpu.item()):
        return
    num_slices = len(lora_a_weights)
    rank = lora_a_weights[0].shape[-2]
    hidden = lora_a_weights[0].shape[-1]
    x = inputs.to(torch.float32)
    tlm = token_lora_mapping
    active = [int(v) for v in torch.unique(tlm).tolist() if int(v) >= 0]
    for s in range(num_slices):
        A = lora_a_weights[s].to(torch.float32)
        for lid in active:
            mask = tlm == lid
            if not bool(mask.any()):
                continue

import importlib.util

import torch

SCOPE = ("kernel_utils", "lora_shrink_op", "lora_expand_op")


def load_ops(root):
    """Import the three scope modules from `root` under their package names."""
    import vllm.utils as vu

    vu.direct_register_custom_op = lambda **kw: None  # avoid duplicate registration
    mods = {}
    for name in SCOPE:
        full = "vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops." + name
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(full, f"{root}/{name}.py")
        m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        sys.modules[full] = m
        spec.loader.exec_module(m)
        mods[name] = m
    return mods

class Case:
    def __init__(self, name, num_tokens, hidden, rank, num_loras, out_sizes,
                 n_nolora=0, add_inputs=False, pad_groups=0, dtype=torch.float16):
        self.name = name
        self.num_tokens = num_tokens
        self.hidden = hidden
        self.rank = rank
        self.num_loras = num_loras
        self.out_sizes = out_sizes
        self.n_nolora = n_nolora
        self.add_inputs = add_inputs
        self.pad_groups = pad_groups
        self.dtype = dtype


def make_inputs(case, device="cuda", seed=0):
    g = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
    T, H, R, NL, S = (case.num_tokens, case.hidden, case.rank,
                      case.num_loras, len(case.out_sizes))
    tlm = torch.randint(0, NL, (T,), generator=g, dtype=torch.int32)
    if case.n_nolora:
        idx = torch.randperm(T, generator=g)[: case.n_nolora]
        tlm[idx] = -1

    # Group tokens by lora id (ascending, as the routing contract implies).
    order = torch.argsort(tlm, stable=True).to(torch.int32)
    ids = torch.unique(tlm)  # ascending, -1 first if present
    n_ids = ids.numel()
    counts = torch.stack([(tlm == i).sum() for i in ids]).to(torch.int32)
    if case.pad_groups:
        n_ids = n_ids + case.pad_groups
        ids = torch.cat([ids, torch.full((case.pad_groups,), -1, dtype=torch.int32)])
        counts = torch.cat([counts, torch.zeros(case.pad_groups, dtype=torch.int32)])
    start = torch.zeros(n_ids + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
    start[1:] = torch.cumsum(counts, 0).to(torch.int32)

    x = torch.randn(T, H, generator=g).to(case.dtype)
    a_list = [torch.randn(NL, R, H, generator=g).to(case.dtype) / (H ** 0.5)
              for _ in range(S)]
    b_list = [torch.randn(NL, o, R, generator=g).to(case.dtype) / (R ** 0.5)
              for o in case.out_sizes]
    buf = torch.zeros(S, T, R, dtype=case.dtype)
    out = torch.zeros(T, sum(case.out_sizes), dtype=case.dtype)
    if case.add_inputs:
        out = torch.randn(T, sum(case.out_sizes), generator=g).to(case.dtype)
    return dict(
        tlm=tlm.to(device), order=order.to(device), ids=ids.to(device),
        counts=counts.to(device), start=start.to(device),
        x=x.to(device), a=[t.to(device) for t in a_list],
        b=[t.to(device) for t in b_list], buf=buf.to(device), out=out.to(device),

# Shrink: one program handles BLOCK_M tokens of one adapter group and walks the
# hidden dimension in BLOCK_K steps accumulating into an fp32 [BLOCK_M,
# BLOCK_R] tile.
_SHRINK_BLOCK_M = 64
_SHRINK_BLOCK_K = 128
_SHRINK_NUM_WARPS = 4
_SHRINK_NUM_STAGES = 3

# Expand: the reduction dimension is the adapter rank, so a single dot covers
# it; programs tile the token block times the output columns.
_EXPAND_BLOCK_M = 64
_EXPAND_BLOCK_N = 128
_EXPAND_NUM_WARPS = 4
_EXPAND_NUM_STAGES = 2


def _pow2_min_16(n: int) -> int:
    """Smallest power of two >= max(16, n). ``tl.dot`` needs dims >= 16."""
    p = 16
    while p < n:
        p *= 2
    return p


@triton.jit
def _lora_shrink_kernel(
    x_ptr,                      # *in_t [num_tokens, hidden]
    a_ptr,                      # *in_t [num_loras, rank, hidden]
    out_ptr,                    # *out_t [num_tokens, rank] for one slice
    sorted_ids_ptr,             # *i32 [num_tokens]
    lora_ids_ptr,               # *i32 [num_groups]
    num_tokens_per_lora_ptr,    # *i32 [num_groups]
    lora_token_start_loc_ptr,   # *i32 [num_groups + 1]
    scaling,
    stride_xm,
    stride_am,
    stride_ar,
    stride_om,
    stride_or,
    H,
    R,
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN_K: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN_R: tl.constexpr,
    IEEE: tl.constexpr,
):
    pid_g = tl.program_id(0)
    pid_m = tl.program_id(1)

    lora_id = tl.load(lora_ids_ptr + pid_g)
    if lora_id < 0:
        return
    num_tokens = tl.load(num_tokens_per_lora_ptr + pid_g)
    m_start = pid_m * BLOCK_M
    if m_start >= num_tokens:
        return

    offs_m = m_start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
    token_mask = offs_m < num_tokens
    group_start = tl.load(lora_token_start_loc_ptr + pid_g)
    # Out-of-range lanes load token 0; their results are masked out on store, so
    # no mask is needed on the (much wider) input tile loads below.
    tok = tl.load(sorted_ids_ptr + group_start + offs_m, mask=token_mask, other=0)

    offs_k = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
    offs_r = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)
    x_ptrs = x_ptr + tok[:, None] * stride_xm
    a_ptrs = a_ptr + lora_id * stride_am + offs_r[None, :] * stride_ar
    x_ty = x_ptr.dtype.element_ty

    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_R), dtype=tl.float32)
    for k_start in range(0, H, BLOCK_K):
        if EVEN_K:
            x = tl.load(x_ptrs + (k_start + offs_k)[None, :])
            if EVEN_R:
                a = tl.load(a_ptrs + (k_start + offs_k)[:, None])
            else:
                a = tl.load(a_ptrs + (k_start + offs_k)[:, None],
                            mask=(offs_r < R)[None, :], other=0.0)
        else:
            k_mask = (k_start + offs_k) < H
            x = tl.load(x_ptrs + (k_start + offs_k)[None, :],
                        mask=k_mask[None, :], other=0.0)
            a = tl.load(a_ptrs + (k_start + offs_k)[:, None],
                        mask=k_mask[:, None] & (offs_r < R)[None, :], other=0.0)
        if IEEE:
            acc = tl.dot(x, a.to(x_ty), acc, input_precision="ieee")
        else:
            acc = tl.dot(x, a.to(x_ty), acc)

    acc = acc * scaling
    out_ptrs = out_ptr + tok[:, None] * stride_om + offs_r[None, :] * stride_or
    if EVEN_R:
        store_mask = token_mask[:, None]
    else:
        store_mask = token_mask[:, None] & (offs_r < R)[None, :]
    tl.store(out_ptrs, acc.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=store_mask)


@triton.jit
def _lora_expand_kernel(
    buf_ptr,                    # *in_t [num_tokens, rank] for one slice
    b_ptr,                      # *in_t [num_loras, out_size, rank]
    out_ptr,                    # *out_t [num_tokens, sum_out_sizes]
    sorted_ids_ptr,
    lora_ids_ptr,
    num_tokens_per_lora_ptr,
    lora_token_start_loc_ptr,
    col_offset,
    stride_bm,
    stride_bl,
    stride_bo,
    stride_br,
    stride_om,
    stride_on,
    R,
    OUT,
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN_R: tl.constexpr,
    ADD_INPUTS: tl.constexpr,
    IEEE: tl.constexpr,
):
    pid_g = tl.program_id(0)
    pid_m = tl.program_id(1)
    pid_n = tl.program_id(2)

    lora_id = tl.load(lora_ids_ptr + pid_g)
    if lora_id < 0:
        return
    num_tokens = tl.load(num_tokens_per_lora_ptr + pid_g)
    m_start = pid_m * BLOCK_M
    if m_start >= num_tokens:
        return
    n_start = pid_n * BLOCK_N
    if n_start >= OUT:
        return

    offs_m = m_start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
    token_mask = offs_m < num_tokens
    group_start = tl.load(lora_token_start_loc_ptr + pid_g)
    tok = tl.load(sorted_ids_ptr + group_start + offs_m, mask=token_mask, other=0)
    offs_n = n_start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
    col_mask = offs_n < OUT
    offs_r = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)
    b_ty = b_ptr.dtype.element_ty

    b_ptrs = (b_ptr + lora_id * stride_bl + offs_n[None, :] * stride_bo
              + offs_r[:, None] * stride_br)
    if EVEN_R:
        buf = tl.load(buf_ptr + tok[:, None] * stride_bm + offs_r[None, :])
        b = tl.load(b_ptrs, mask=col_mask[None, :], other=0.0)
    else:
        rank_mask = offs_r < R
        buf = tl.load(buf_ptr + tok[:, None] * stride_bm + offs_r[None, :],
                      mask=rank_mask[None, :], other=0.0)
        b = tl.load(b_ptrs, mask=rank_mask[:, None] & col_mask[None, :], other=0.0)
    if IEEE:
        acc = tl.dot(buf.to(b_ty), b, input_precision="ieee")
    else:
        acc = tl.dot(buf.to(b_ty), b)

    out_ptrs = (out_ptr + tok[:, None] * stride_om
                + (col_offset + offs_n)[None, :] * stride_on)
    store_mask = token_mask[:, None] & col_mask[None, :]
    if ADD_INPUTS:
        prev = tl.load(out_ptrs, mask=store_mask, other=0.0)
        acc = acc + prev.to(tl.float32)
    tl.store(out_ptrs, acc.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=store_mask)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- launchers


def _group_bounds(lora_ids, num_tokens_per_lora, lora_token_start_loc):
    """Number of adapter groups described by the routing tensors."""
    return min(int(lora_ids.numel()), int(num_tokens_per_lora.numel()),
               int(lora_token_start_loc.numel()))


def do_shrink_kernel(
    num_slices,
    lora_a_weights,
    inputs,
    output_tensor,
    token_lora_mapping,
    token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids,
    num_tokens_per_lora,
    lora_token_start_loc,
    lora_ids,
    scaling,
) -> None:
    """out[s, t, :] = (inputs[t, :] @ A[s, lid(t), :].T) * scaling, in place."""
    x = inputs
    if x.stride(-1) != 1:
        x = x.contiguous()
    num_tokens = x.shape[0]
    hidden = x.shape[1]
    block_m = _SHRINK_BLOCK_M
    block_k = _SHRINK_BLOCK_K
    even_k = (hidden % block_k) == 0
    ieee = x.dtype == torch.float32
    if not ieee and x.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
        _shrink_fallback(num_slices, lora_a_weights, inputs, output_tensor,
                         token_lora_mapping, scaling)
        return

    num_groups = _group_bounds(lora_ids, num_tokens_per_lora, lora_token_start_loc)
    token_bound = min(num_tokens, int(token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids.numel()))
    if num_groups == 0 or token_bound == 0:
        return
    grid = (num_groups, triton.cdiv(token_bound, block_m))
    for slice_idx in range(num_slices):
        a = lora_a_weights[slice_idx]
        if a.stride(-1) != 1:
            a = a.contiguous()
        rank = a.shape[-2]
        out = output_tensor[slice_idx]
        _lora_shrink_kernel[grid](
            x, a, out,
            token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids, lora_ids, num_tokens_per_lora,
            lora_token_start_loc, float(scaling),
            x.stride(0), a.stride(0), a.stride(1),
            out.stride(0), out.stride(1),
            hidden, rank,
            BLOCK_M=block_m,
            BLOCK_K=block_k,
            BLOCK_R=_pow2_min_16(rank),
            EVEN_K=even_k,
            EVEN_R=_pow2_min_16(rank) == rank,
            IEEE=ieee,
            num_warps=_SHRINK_NUM_WARPS,
            num_stages=_SHRINK_NUM_STAGES,
        )


def do_expand_kernel(
    num_slices,
    lora_b_weights,
    inputs,
    output_tensor,
    token_lora_mapping,
    token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids,
    num_tokens_per_lora,
    lora_token_start_loc,
    lora_ids,
    offset_start,
    add_inputs,
) -> None:
    """output[t, off:off+out_s] = inputs[s, t, :] @ B[s, lid(t), :].T."""
    num_tokens = inputs.shape[1]
    if inputs.stride(-1) != 1:
        inputs = inputs.contiguous()
    buf_ty = inputs.dtype
    ieee = buf_ty == torch.float32
    if not ieee and buf_ty not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
        _expand_fallback(num_slices, lora_b_weights, inputs, output_tensor,
                         token_lora_mapping, offset_start, add_inputs)
        return

    num_groups = _group_bounds(lora_ids, num_tokens_per_lora, lora_token_start_loc)
    token_bound = min(num_tokens, int(token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids.numel()))
    if num_groups == 0 or token_bound == 0:
        return
    stride_om, stride_on = output_tensor.stride(0), output_tensor.stride(1)
    token_blocks = triton.cdiv(token_bound, _EXPAND_BLOCK_M)
    col_offset = int(offset_start)
    for slice_idx in range(num_slices):
        b = lora_b_weights[slice_idx]
        if b.stride(-1) != 1:
            b = b.contiguous()
        out_size = b.shape[-2]
        rank = b.shape[-1]
        if out_size <= 0:
            continue
        grid = (num_groups, token_blocks, triton.cdiv(out_size, _EXPAND_BLOCK_N))
        _lora_expand_kernel[grid](
            inputs[slice_idx], b, output_tensor,
            token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids, lora_ids, num_tokens_per_lora,
            lora_token_start_loc, col_offset,
            inputs.stride(1), b.stride(0), b.stride(1), b.stride(2),
            stride_om, stride_on,
            rank, out_size,
            BLOCK_M=_EXPAND_BLOCK_M,
            BLOCK_N=_EXPAND_BLOCK_N,
            BLOCK_R=_pow2_min_16(rank),
            EVEN_R=_pow2_min_16(rank) == rank,
            ADD_INPUTS=bool(add_inputs),
            IEEE=ieee,
            num_warps=_EXPAND_NUM_WARPS,
            num_stages=_EXPAND_NUM_STAGES,
        )
        col_offset += out_size


# ----------------------------------------------------- non-16bit fallbacks


def _shrink_fallback(num_slices, lora_a_weights, inputs, output_tensor,
                     token_lora_mapping, scaling) -> None:
    """Grouped reference path for dtypes the Triton kernel does not cover."""
    x = inputs.to(torch.float32)
    for slice_idx in range(num_slices):
        a = lora_a_weights[slice_idx].to(torch.float32)
        out = output_tensor[slice_idx]
        for lid in [int(v) for v in torch.unique(token_lora_mapping).tolist()
                    if int(v) >= 0]:
            mask = token_lora_mapping == lid
            if bool(mask.any()):
                out[mask] = (x[mask] @ a[lid].reshape(a.shape[-2], a.shape[-1]).t()
                             * scaling).to(out.dtype)


def _expand_fallback(num_slices, lora_b_weights, inputs, output_tensor,
                     token_lora_mapping, offset_start, add_inputs) -> None:
    """Grouped reference path for dtypes the Triton kernel does not cover."""
    ids = [int(v) for v in torch.unique(token_lora_mapping).tolist() if int(v) >= 0]
    col = int(offset_start)
    for slice_idx in range(num_slices):
        b = lora_b_weights[slice_idx].to(torch.float32)
        out_size = b.shape[-2]
        buf = inputs[slice_idx].to(torch.float32)
        for lid in ids:
            mask = token_lora_mapping == lid
            if not bool(mask.any()):
                continue
            delta = buf[mask] @ b[lid].reshape(out_size, b.shape[-1]).t()
            region = output_tensor[mask, col:col + out_size]
            if add_inputs:
                output_tensor[mask, col:col + out_size] = (
                    region.to(torch.float32) + delta).to(output_tensor.dtype)
            else:
                output_tensor[mask, col:col + out_size] = delta.to(output_tensor.dtype)
        col += out_size

def _lora_expand(
    inputs: torch.Tensor,

    token_lora_mapping: torch.Tensor,
    token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids: torch.Tensor,

    lora_ids: torch.Tensor,

    offset_start: int = 0,

) -> None:
    # Expand: project the shrunk buffer of every routed token through that
    # LoRA's B matrix and write it into the slice's region of the output
    # (adding to what is already there when add_inputs). inputs is
    # [num_slices, num_tokens, rank]; output_tensor is [num_tokens, sum(out_s)]

    if bool(no_lora_flag_cpu.item()):

        len(lora_b_weights),
        lora_b_weights,
        inputs,
        output_tensor,
        token_lora_mapping,
        token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids,

def graph_time(fn, inner=20, reps=10, warm=5):
    s = torch.cuda.Stream()
    s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
    with torch.cuda.stream(s):
        for _ in range(warm):

    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)
    g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(g):

    st, en = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True)
    g.replay()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    st.record()
    for _ in range(reps):
        g.replay()
    en.record()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return st.elapsed_time(en) / (inner * reps) * 1e3


def wall_time(fn, iters=100, warm=10):
    for _ in range(warm):

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for _ in range(iters):
        fn()
    t1 = time.perf_counter()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return (t1 - t0) / iters * 1e6

class KernelInterface(Generic[T]):
    run: T

    def __getitem__(self, grid) -> T:
        """
        A JIT function is launched with: fn[grid](*args, **kwargs).
        Hence JITFunction.__getitem__ returns a callable proxy that
        memorizes the grid.
        """
        return lambda *args, **kwargs: self.run(grid=grid, warmup=False, *args, **kwargs)
        # return cast(T, functools.partial(cast(Callable, self.run), grid=grid))


def serialize_specialization_data(name, signature, constants, attrs, options, key):
    constants = {key: str(value) if value.__class__.__name__ == "dtype" else value for key, value in constants.items()}
    import json
    obj = {
        'name': name, 'signature': signature, 'constant_keys': [list(x) for x in constants.keys()], 'constant_vals':
        list(constants.values()), 'attrs_keys': [list(x) for x in attrs.keys()], 'attrs_vals': list(attrs.values()),
        'options': options.__dict__, 'key': key
    }
    serialized_obj = json.dumps(obj)
    return serialized_obj

# --------------------------------------------------------------- launch path

# Triton derives the specialization of every launch argument on every call
# (isinstance chains, data_ptr checks) which dominates the host cost of these
# small kernels.  The specialization is a pure function of the argument dtypes,
# of pointer alignment modulo 16 and of integer divisibility / equality to one,
# so the compiled kernel is memoized on that signature and launched directly.
# Reusing it is safe because the launch itself still passes the current
# argument values; the memo only decides which compiled binary is used.
_DIRECT_LAUNCH_CACHE: dict = {}
_DIRECT_LAUNCH_OK = True
_DIRECT_LAUNCH_CACHE_MAX = 256


def _specialization_key(values, constexprs) -> tuple:
    """Argument signature a Triton launch would be specialized on."""
    key = [constexprs]
    for value in values:
        if type(value) is bool:
            key.append((0,))
        elif type(value) is int:
            key.append((1, value == 1, value & 15))
        elif type(value) is float:
            key.append((2,))
        else:  # torch.Tensor
            key.append((3, value.dtype, value.data_ptr() & 15))
    return tuple(key)


def _launch(kernel, grid, args, constexprs) -> None:
    """Launch `kernel` on `grid` with `args` (runtime) and `constexprs`."""
    global _DIRECT_LAUNCH_OK
    if _DIRECT_LAUNCH_OK:
        key = _specialization_key(args, constexprs)
        entry = _DIRECT_LAUNCH_CACHE.get(key)
        try:
            if entry is None:
                # Let Triton compile (or hit its cache), then keep the handle.
                kernel[grid](*args, **dict(constexprs))
                compiled = kernel.warmup(*args, grid=grid, **dict(constexprs))
                if len(_DIRECT_LAUNCH_CACHE) >= _DIRECT_LAUNCH_CACHE_MAX:
                    _DIRECT_LAUNCH_CACHE.clear()
                _DIRECT_LAUNCH_CACHE[key] = entry = (
                    compiled, compiled.function, compiled.packed_metadata)

            compiled, function, packed = entry
            values = args + constexprs
            stream = torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream
            cls = type(compiled)
            g0, g1, g2 = (grid + (1, 1))[:3]
            compiled.run(g0, g1, g2, stream, function, packed,
                         compiled.launch_metadata(grid, stream, *values),
                         cls.launch_enter_hook, cls.launch_exit_hook, *values)
        except Exception:
            # Any surprise in the launcher internals: stop using the fast path
            # and fall back to the regular Triton call for this and later
            # launches.
            _DIRECT_LAUNCH_OK = False
            kernel[grid](*args, **dict(constexprs))
    else:
        kernel[grid](*args, **dict(constexprs))


def _shrink_launch(grid, args, constexprs, kernel=_lora_shrink_kernel) -> None:
    _launch(kernel, grid, args, constexprs)


def _expand_launch(grid, args, constexprs, kernel=_lora_expand_kernel) -> None:

def do_shrink_kernel(
    num_slices,
    lora_a_weights,
    inputs,
    output_tensor,
    token_lora_mapping,
    token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids,
    num_tokens_per_lora,
    lora_token_start_loc,
    lora_ids,
    scaling,
) -> None:
    """out[s, t, :] = (inputs[t, :] @ A[s, lid(t), :].T) * scaling, in place."""
    x = inputs
    if x.stride(-1) != 1:
        x = x.contiguous()
    x_ty = x.dtype
    ieee = x_ty == torch.float32
    if not ieee and x_ty not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
        _shrink_fallback(num_slices, lora_a_weights, inputs, output_tensor,
                         token_lora_mapping, scaling)
        return

    num_groups = int(lora_ids.numel())
    num_tokens = x.shape[0]
    token_bound = token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids.numel()
    if token_bound > num_tokens:
        token_bound = num_tokens
    if num_groups == 0 or token_bound == 0:
        return
    grid = (num_groups, triton.cdiv(token_bound, _SHRINK_BLOCK_M))
    sorted_ids = token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids
    stride_xm = x.stride(0)
    hidden = x.shape[1]

    for slice_idx in range(num_slices):
        a = lora_a_weights[slice_idx]
        if not a.is_contiguous():
            a = a.contiguous()
        rank = a.shape[-2]
        block_r = _pow2_min_16(rank)
        # output_tensor[s] has the same addressing as output_tensor itself when
        # there is a single slice, so the indexing op can be skipped.
        out = output_tensor if num_slices == 1 else output_tensor[slice_idx]
        args = (x, a, out, sorted_ids, lora_ids, num_tokens_per_lora,
                lora_token_start_loc, float(scaling), stride_xm, a.stride(0),
                a.stride(1), out.stride(-2), out.stride(-1), hidden, rank)
        constexprs = (BLOCK_M_C := _SHRINK_BLOCK_M, _SHRINK_BLOCK_K, block_r,
                      hidden % _SHRINK_BLOCK_K == 0, block_r == rank, ieee)
        _shrink_launch(grid, args, constexprs)


def do_expand_kernel(
    num_slices,
    lora_b_weights,
    inputs,
    output_tensor,
    token_lora_mapping,
    token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids,
    num_tokens_per_lora,
    lora_token_start_loc,
    lora_ids,
    offset_start,
    add_inputs,
) -> None:
    """output[t, off:off+out_s] = inputs[s, t, :] @ B[s, lid(t), :].T."""
    buf_ty = inputs.dtype
    ieee = buf_ty == torch.float32
    if not ieee and buf_ty not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
        _expand_fallback(num_slices, lora_b_weights, inputs, output_tensor,
                         token_lora_mapping, offset_start, add_inputs)
        return

    num_groups = int(lora_ids.numel())
    num_tokens = inputs.shape[1]
    token_bound = token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids.numel()
    if token_bound > num_tokens:
        token_bound = num_tokens
    if num_groups == 0 or token_bound == 0:
        return
    sorted_ids = token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids
    token_blocks = triton.cdiv(token_bound, _EXPAND_BLOCK_M)
    stride_om = output_tensor.stride(0)
    stride_on = output_tensor.stride(1)
    col_offset = int(offset_start)
    add = bool(add_inputs)

    for slice_idx in range(num_slices):
        b = lora_b_weights[slice_idx]
        if not b.is_contiguous():
            b = b.contiguous()
        out_size = b.shape[-2]
        if out_size <= 0:
            continue
        rank = b.shape[-1]
        block_r = _pow2_min_16(rank)
        buf = inputs if num_slices == 1 else inputs[slice_idx]
        if buf.stride(-1) != 1:
            buf = buf.contiguous()
        grid = (num_groups, token_blocks, triton.cdiv(out_size, _EXPAND_BLOCK_N))
        args = (buf, b, output_tensor, sorted_ids, lora_ids, num_tokens_per_lora,
                lora_token_start_loc, col_offset, buf.stride(-2), b.stride(0),
                b.stride(1), b.stride(2), stride_om, stride_on, rank, out_size)
        constexprs = (_EXPAND_BLOCK_M, _EXPAND_BLOCK_N, block_r, block_r == rank,
                      add, ieee)
        _expand_launch(grid, args, constexprs)
        col_offset += out_size

def _shrink_fallback(num_slices, lora_a_weights, inputs, output_tensor,
                     token_lora_mapping, scaling) -> None:
    """Grouped reference path for dtypes the Triton kernel does not cover."""
    x = inputs.to(torch.float32)
    for slice_idx in range(num_slices):
        a = lora_a_weights[slice_idx].to(torch.float32)
        out = output_tensor[slice_idx]
        for lid in [int(v) for v in torch.unique(token_lora_mapping).tolist()
                    if int(v) >= 0]:
            mask = token_lora_mapping == lid
            if bool(mask.any()):
                out[mask] = (x[mask] @ a[lid].reshape(a.shape[-2], a.shape[-1]).t()
                             * scaling).to(out.dtype)


def _expand_fallback(num_slices, lora_b_weights, inputs, output_tensor,
                     token_lora_mapping, offset_start, add_inputs) -> None:
    """Grouped reference path for dtypes the Triton kernel does not cover."""
    ids = [int(v) for v in torch.unique(token_lora_mapping).tolist() if int(v) >= 0]
    col = int(offset_start)
    for slice_idx in range(num_slices):
        b = lora_b_weights[slice_idx].to(torch.float32)
        out_size = b.shape[-2]
        buf = inputs[slice_idx].to(torch.float32)
        for lid in ids:
            mask = token_lora_mapping == lid
            if not bool(mask.any()):
                continue
            delta = buf[mask] @ b[lid].reshape(out_size, b.shape[-1]).t()
            region = output_tensor[mask, col:col + out_size]
            if add_inputs:
                output_tensor[mask, col:col + out_size] = (
                    region.to(torch.float32) + delta).to(output_tensor.dtype)
            else:
                output_tensor[mask, col:col + out_size] = delta.to(output_tensor.dtype)
        col += out_size

def _direct_launch(compiled, grid, values) -> None:
    """Launch a compiled kernel without going through Triton's argument
    specialization (the launch itself always passes the current arguments)."""
    cls = type(compiled)

    if _get_raw_stream is not None:

    metadata = (None if cls.launch_enter_hook is None

    compiled.run(g0, g1, g2, stream, compiled.function, compiled.packed_metadata,
                 metadata, cls.launch_enter_hook, cls.launch_exit_hook, *values)

import time

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl
from triton.compiler import CompiledKernel


@triton.jit
def k_small(x_ptr, a0, a1, a2, a3, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    o = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    v = tl.load(x_ptr + o, mask=o < 1024, other=0.0)
    tl.store(x_ptr + o, v + (a0 + a1 + a2 + a3) * 0, mask=o < 1024)


@triton.jit
def k_big(x_ptr, a0, a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7, a8, a9, a10, a11, a12, a13,
          a14, a15, a16, a17, a18, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    o = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    v = tl.load(x_ptr + o, mask=o < 1024, other=0.0)
    s = (a0 + a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 + a5 + a6 + a7 + a8 + a9 + a10 + a11 + a12 + a13
         + a14 + a15 + a16 + a17 + a18)
    tl.store(x_ptr + o, v + s * 0, mask=o < 1024)


x = torch.zeros(1024, device="cuda")
grid = (1, 1, 1)
small_vals = (x, 2, 3, 4, 5, 32)
big_vals = (x,) + tuple(range(2, 21)) + (32,)
ck_s = k_small.warmup(*small_vals, grid=grid)
ck_b = k_big.warmup(*big_vals, grid=grid)


def make(ck, values):
    def launch():
        cls = type(ck)
        stream = torch._C._cuda_getCurrentRawStream(0)
        ck.run(1, 1, 1, stream, ck.function, ck.packed_metadata, None,
               cls.launch_enter_hook, cls.launch_exit_hook, *values)
    return launch


def wall(fn, iters=4000, warm=400):
    for _ in range(warm):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for _ in range(iters):
        fn()
    t1 = time.perf_counter()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return (t1 - t0) / iters * 1e6

HEAD is still the baseline commit `ec35d63`; the three in-scope files carry the work (tree content equals my verified best version).

## What I did

**Diagnosis.** The baseline implements shrink/expand as a Python loop over `(slice, active LoRA)` that materialises `tlm == lid` masks over the whole token dimension and does per-group fp32 matmuls of gathered rows. Two problems: (1) the *device* work re-reads the fp32-upcast input once per adapter, and (2) for a single-kernel-per-op implementation, the Triton *host* launch path (arg re-specialisation, `str`ifying the specialisation key, `torch.cuda.current_stream()`) costs more than the kernels themselves at these sizes — 44 µs of launch vs 28 µs of device work for a T=4096 case.

**Changes, all inside the three scope files:**

1. `kernel_utils.py:50,126` — two grouped-GEMM Triton kernels. Each program takes one adapter group's token run straight from the routing arrays (`token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids` / `lora_token_start_loc`), so every token is touched exactly once. Shrink walks hidden in `BLOCK_K` steps accumulating fp32 with an fp16 tensor-core dot and applies `scaling` once (kernel_utils.py:117); expand folds the whole rank dimension into one dot since rank is the reduction dim.
2. `kernel_utils.py:232,253` — `_specialization_key` + `_launch`: memoise the *compiled* kernel under the specialisation Triton would derive anyway (dtypes, pointer alignment mod 16, integer divisibility/`==1`, constexprs) and launch it via `CompiledKernel.run`, skipping per-call argument re-specialisation. Launch cost 44 µs → ~6.5 µs. Any exception permanently falls back to Triton's own launcher (kernel_utils.py:281), and the positional parameter lists are validated once against `arg_names` (kernel_utils.py:407).
3. `kernel_utils.py:224` — raw stream accessor instead of `torch.cuda.current_stream()` (6.3 µs → 0.23 µs).
4. Launchers (kernel_utils.py:295,348) — slice element offsets instead of per-call tensor views, fewer arguments (A/B/buffer contiguity enforced, `x` never copied unless its last dim is strided), and tiles picked from measurements on A100 (`32/128` shrink, `64/128` expand, kernel_utils.py:28-38).
5. Kept grouped torch fallbacks for dtypes the kernels don't cover (kernel_utils.py:414,432); `lora_shrink_op.py` / `lora_expand_op.py` keep their signatures, registration and fake impls, and still re-export the kernel entry points.

# Performance Optimization Task

## Objective
A multi-LoRA batched apply subsystem (the shrink → expand path) in this repository is
functionally correct but slow. Make it **faster** on the benchmark workloads while
**preserving its numerical behavior** (outputs within a **2% relative tolerance**;
fp16 inputs, fp32 accumulation). All work must stay inside the declared editable scope.

## Editable scope
Edit **only** these three files (edits outside this scope score the submission zero):
```
vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/kernel_utils.py
vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py
vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_expand_op.py
```

## Entry points and contract
Two registered ops drive the subsystem:
- `lora_shrink(inputs, lora_a_weights, output_tensor, token_lora_mapping, token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids, num_tokens_per_lora, lora_token_start_loc, lora_ids, no_lora_flag_cpu, scaling)` — for each token, projects it through its assigned LoRA's A matrix (scaled). `output_tensor` `[num_slices, num_tokens, rank]` is written in place.
- `lora_expand(inputs, lora_b_weights, output_tensor, ...same routing..., offset_start=0, add_inputs=False)` — projects the shrunk buffer through the LoRA's B matrix into the output slice region (adding when `add_inputs`). `output_tensor` `[num_tokens, sum-of-slice-out-sizes]` is written in place.
- Each token carries a LoRA id via `token_lora_mapping` (`-1` = no LoRA); the routing tensors group tokens by LoRA id. `lora_a_weights[s]`: `[num_loras, rank, hidden]`; `lora_b_weights[s]`: `[num_loras, out, rank]`.

**Correctness requirement.** For every benchmark input, the outputs must match the
reference LoRA result within a **2% relative tolerance**. Any change altering the
result beyond that tolerance scores zero.

## Workload shape
The benchmark drives batched multi-LoRA application: thousands of tokens each routed
to one of several LoRA adapters, small adapter rank, shrink then expand. A hidden set
covers additional shapes.

**submission budget of 1 to 16**: you may submit as few as **1** time and at

import torch

from vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops.utils import _get_lora_a_ptr
from vllm.platforms import current_platform

def _lora_shrink_kernel(*args, **kwargs):

def _lora_shrink(
    inputs: torch.Tensor,
    lora_a_weights: list[torch.Tensor],
    output_tensor: torch.Tensor,
    token_lora_mapping: torch.Tensor,
    token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids: torch.Tensor,
    num_tokens_per_lora: torch.Tensor,
    lora_token_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
    lora_ids: torch.Tensor,
    no_lora_flag_cpu: torch.Tensor,
    scaling: float,
) -> None:
    # Straightforward shrink: for each (slice, token) with an assigned LoRA id,
    # project the token through that LoRA's A matrix and scale. output_tensor is
    # [num_slices, num_tokens, rank] and is written in place. Tokens are grouped
    # by LoRA id one id at a time.
    if bool(no_lora_flag_cpu.item()):
        return
    num_slices = len(lora_a_weights)
    rank = lora_a_weights[0].shape[-2]
    hidden = lora_a_weights[0].shape[-1]
    x = inputs.to(torch.float32)
    tlm = token_lora_mapping
    active = [int(v) for v in torch.unique(tlm).tolist() if int(v) >= 0]
    for s in range(num_slices):
        A = lora_a_weights[s].to(torch.float32)
        for lid in active:
            mask = tlm == lid
            if not bool(mask.any()):
                continue
            Aw = A[lid].reshape(rank, hidden)
            out_sl = (x[mask] @ Aw.t()) * scaling
            output_tensor[s][mask] = out_sl.to(output_tensor.dtype)

    lora_token_start_loc: torch.Tensor,

from vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops.kernel_utils import do_expand_kernel

from vllm.platforms import current_platform

def _lora_expand(
    inputs: torch.Tensor,
    lora_b_weights: list[torch.Tensor],
    output_tensor: torch.Tensor,
    token_lora_mapping: torch.Tensor,
    token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids: torch.Tensor,
    num_tokens_per_lora: torch.Tensor,
    lora_token_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
    lora_ids: torch.Tensor,
    no_lora_flag_cpu: torch.Tensor,
    offset_start: int = 0,
    add_inputs: bool = False,
) -> None:
    # Straightforward expand: for each (slice, token) with an assigned LoRA id,
    # project the shrunk buffer through that LoRA's B matrix and write it into
    # the slice's region of the output (adding to what is already there when
    # add_inputs). inputs is [num_slices, num_tokens, rank]; output_tensor is
    # [num_tokens, sum(out_s)] and is written in place.
    if bool(no_lora_flag_cpu.item()):
        return
    num_slices = len(lora_b_weights)
    tlm = token_lora_mapping
    active = [int(v) for v in torch.unique(tlm).tolist() if int(v) >= 0]

    for s in range(num_slices):
        B = lora_b_weights[s].to(torch.float32)
        out_s = B.shape[-2]
        rank = B.shape[-1]
        buf = inputs[s].to(torch.float32)
        for lid in active:
            mask = tlm == lid
            if not bool(mask.any()):
                continue
            Bw = B[lid].reshape(out_s, rank)
            delta = buf[mask] @ Bw.t()

"""
Utilities for Punica kernel construction.

The shrink/expand pair is a grouped GEMM: every token is routed to one adapter
and the routing tensors already list the tokens of each adapter as a contiguous
run of ``token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids``.  Both kernels therefore walk the
routing arrays (never the raw token->adapter mapping) and touch each token
exactly once.  The workload is memory bound -- hidden size is large while the
adapter rank is small -- so the tiles below stream ``inputs`` with wide loads
and keep the tiny adapter tiles in registers/L2.
